decision_question: Is ReFolDec ready, within its stated scope, to be treated as a usable, safe, and evidence-supported recursive fold/unfold framework, and what may be released now versus what must defer for evidence?
acceptance_criteria: Classify material claims as confirmed, inferred, proposal, or unknown with exact evidence paths and line ranges.
Separate analytical structural evidence, live command evidence, historical benchmark evidence, and not-run work.
Record a smallest decisive next test, owner decision, and consequence for every blocked claim.
State usable-now, approved-with-limits, and defer-for-evidence boundaries.
Keep placeholder URLs and unsupported runtime claims explicitly unverified.
constraints: No codec runtime implementation or four-representation contract change.
No external publication, organ contact, or placeholder URL verification.
No source-document rewriting to strengthen the maturity result.
No external provider, protected holdout, renderer, client, or domain-specialist adjudication was available.

evidence_taxonomy.analytical: Contracts, documentation, static inspection, and reviewer reasoning.
evidence_taxonomy.live: Commands actually run on the frozen repository; limited to registry validation, tests, and diff hygiene.
evidence_taxonomy.historical: Earlier evaluation/benchmark records retained for context and not treated as current live proof.
evidence_taxonomy.not-run: A fold, inverse fold, round-trip, renderer, external conformance, portability, or whole-tree publication test not performed.

shared_model_or_source_limits: Evidence, outcome, and safety/portability reviewers used separate prompts and contexts but the same local, self-authored source set.
The model family was not independently known.
The equilibrium skill's own evaluation and benchmark records were among the reviewed sources.
No independent external source, live fold executor, external provider, protected holdout, renderer, or domain-specialist adjudication was available.

initial_reviews.tools_permissions: read-only repository review; no side effects
initial_reviews.finding: Contracts and vocabulary are directly supported; practical losslessness, round trips, organ conformance, and portability are not evidenced.

initial_reviews.tools_permissions: read-only repository review; no side effects
initial_reviews.finding: The repository is useful as a specification/head-canon and planning reference, but the case study is illustrative and release language needs explicit limits.

initial_reviews.tools_permissions: read-only repository review; no side effects
initial_reviews.finding: The firewall is policy and partial automation, not whole-tree clearance; placeholders, unsupported folds, runtime assumptions, and client portability remain bounded risks.

claim_ledger.claim: ReFolDec is defined as a capture-first framework for turning thoughts, workflows, narratives, and repeated actions into structured, visual, reusable, and versioned artifacts.
claim_ledger.consequence: The public positioning would overstate the repository's actual concern.
claim_ledger.next_test: Trace one owner-authorized input through the claimed artifact types and record outputs and limitations.

claim_ledger.claim: Meaning can move recursively between representations without loss of semantic continuity.
claim_ledger.consequence: The central recursive codec thesis would fail for at least one transformation.
claim_ledger.next_test: Execute the invariant-preserving fixture loop described for CLM-07.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Present this as a design thesis, not an observed result.

claim_ledger.claim: ReFolDec is a Git-backed specification/contract repository and does not currently contain an application runtime.
claim_ledger.consequence: Treating prose contracts as an executable codec would mislead users and release decisions.
claim_ledger.next_test: Inspect the frozen tree and run the declared checks; do not make a runtime claim without an actual tested runtime surface.

claim_ledger.claim: ReFolDec defines a bidirectional model: xME is maturation/fold, xIE is inversion/unfold, and xMIE is the combined mechanic.
claim_ledger.consequence: Inconsistent vocabulary would prevent shared coordination across organs.
claim_ledger.next_test: Compare downstream organ terminology with the canonical vocabulary.

claim_ledger.claim: There are exactly four canonical representations: Diagram, Code, Documentation, and Agent-Executable.
claim_ledger.next_test: Run a static conformance scan across organ contracts and artifacts.

claim_ledger.claim: The head-and-organs model, ownership boundaries, source-of-truth rule, and conformance rules are defined.
claim_ledger.consequence: Organ drift and cross-fold boundary violations could go undetected.
claim_ledger.next_test: Compare owner-authorized current organ contracts and vendored registry copies with the head.

claim_ledger.claim: The contract enumerates legal reversible fold pairs and explicitly defers direct Diagram to Agent-Executable folds.
claim_ledger.consequence: Implementers may expose unsupported direct transformations.
claim_ledger.next_test: Scan organ implementations for undeclared direct folds and require contract revision before accepting them.

claim_ledger.claim: Losslessness is defined as preservation of semantic roles, node identity, edge topology, flow relationships, and governance tags; layout, palette binding, and prose style may vary.
claim_ledger.consequence: Different organs could preserve different meanings.
claim_ledger.next_test: Compare all five invariant classes before and after each legal fold on one shared fixture.

claim_ledger.claim: ReFolDec currently demonstrates practical lossless and reversible folds with successful round trips.
claim_ledger.consequence: A claimed lossless fold could silently change meaning.
claim_ledger.next_test: Freeze one fixture per legal fold, execute fold and inverse, and compare all invariants.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Keep all practical lossless, reversible, and round-trip claims deferred until fixture results exist.

claim_ledger.claim: The documented case study is evidence that one complete fold/unfold loop has run.
claim_ledger.consequence: Public readers may mistake an illustrative scenario for empirical proof.
claim_ledger.next_test: Archive raw input, every intermediate artifact, final SKILL.md, cross-representation IDs/tags, hashes, and an unfold/refold comparison.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Keep the case study labeled illustrative until a frozen proof fixture is archived.

claim_ledger.claim: The eight-stage core loop and four-representation contract are already one internally aligned formal model.
claim_ledger.consequence: Implementers cannot tell whether idea, text, structure, and reusable artifact are canonical representations or explanatory states.
claim_ledger.next_test: Publish a normative mapping for every loop stage and transition, verify it against the legal-fold table, and run one fixture.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Defer claims of one coherent formal loop until the mapping is resolved without changing the four-representation contract in this task.

claim_ledger.claim: Process Skills are defined as executable capture workflows and checked-in local skills exist.
claim_ledger.consequence: The executable-plane description would overstate the repository contents.
claim_ledger.next_test: Validate each checked-in skill against trigger, output, safety, and portability criteria.

claim_ledger.claim: The local equilibrium-review skill and its evaluation materials prove portable, effective, production-ready agent execution.
claim_ledger.evidence_state: historical and analytical; no live provider run
claim_ledger.consequence: Users may rely on a skill that activates poorly or handles untrusted input unsafely.
claim_ledger.next_test: Run matched live evaluations across separated clients or model families with an unseen holdout and human/domain-specialist grading.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Approve local analytical use only; make no portability, uplift, production, or general task-quality claim.

claim_ledger.claim: The semantic-class registry is a color-agnostic, validated meaning axis for downstream organs.
claim_ledger.evidence_state: live for registry only; analytical for organ use
claim_ledger.consequence: Role meaning and palette governance could drift.
claim_ledger.next_test: Require organ parity checks and verify downstream consumers bind tokens without redefining roles.

claim_ledger.claim: The scope firewall defines publication and privacy boundaries for the ecosystem.
claim_ledger.consequence: Private or proprietary material could enter shared assets.
claim_ledger.next_test: Apply the checklist to every frozen release tree.

claim_ledger.claim: The complete repository is proven safe and publication-ready by the scope firewall.
claim_ledger.consequence: A public release could expose prohibited content or misleading references.
claim_ledger.next_test: Freeze the release tree, run a repository-wide sensitive-content/reference scan, and independently inspect every flagged result and checklist item.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Do not treat policy presence or registry validation as whole-tree publication clearance.

claim_ledger.claim: The organ pointer table and external links are authoritative and verified.
claim_ledger.consequence: Readers may be sent to nonexistent or unauthorized destinations.
claim_ledger.next_test: Run owner-authorized URL and repository checks with retrieval dates.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Retain placeholder labels and do not call links verified.

claim_ledger.claim: Downstream organs conform to ReFolDec contracts and the active/lineage statuses in the ecosystem map are current.
claim_ledger.consequence: The head may describe an ecosystem that has drifted or does not exist as stated.
claim_ledger.next_test: Compare current owner-authorized organ artifacts and record parity/conformance results.
claim_ledger.owner_decision: Treat organ conformance and status as unverified until source snapshots are available.

claim_ledger.claim: The repository's current validation surface supports the narrow specification baseline.
claim_ledger.consequence: The documentation/registry baseline would not be mechanically healthy.
claim_ledger.next_test: Rerun the declared checks on every baseline revision.

falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Execute each legal fold and inverse on frozen fixtures and compare all invariants.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: The case study proves one complete loop.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Archive a complete source-to-skill fixture with hashes and a successful unfold/refold comparison.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: Skill evaluation materials prove portability or readiness.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Run matched live evaluations with separated clients/model families and a protected unseen holdout.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: The scope firewall proves whole-repository publication safety.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Run and record a whole-tree firewall scan plus independent manual review.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: The four-representation contract and eight-stage loop are already aligned.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Publish a normative stage/transition mapping and verify it with one fixture.

test_results: No counterexample was falsified because the decisive runtime, fixture, portability, and whole-tree tests were not available.
The disruptor results are not live proof of defects or correctness; they are analytical objections that preserve deferral.

decisive_evidence: The frozen repository directly defines a coherent vocabulary, four-representation contract, legal-fold boundaries, invariants, registry policy, and scope firewall.
The live registry validator and 21-test suite pass, but their scope is narrow.
The repository explicitly defers the runtime and round-trip test implementation.
The equilibrium benchmark is not-run and the evolution review is analytical with external holdout required.
The representative case study is explicitly not a record of a specific executed event.
The core loop includes stages outside the exhaustive four-representation contract without a normative mapping.
